title: Lake Charles: a man with a forty-five orders the dance to continue
summary: When Fields ends the dance, a man draws a pistol and demands more music; the doorman defuses it, proving Rene Hall's warnings.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: What was the incident of the fellow that wanted you to stop the dance?
That was in Lake Charles, Louisiana, I believe it was.
Why don't you tell us about that.
Before that, and incidentally, that was a date that Harry Burns had booked.

Rene had often said, I've always been a person that if I didn't understand why a person was saying what you said, I would at least ask him, and Rene had said one time, I don't want to go down south with you, and I said, I'm in the south and he said, but it's a little different. He said Oklahoma may be south, but it's not like the deep south and I said why? He said the way I talk to white people. I said do I talk to them wrong? He said no, you don't talk to them wrong, but the way they feel, you're just not supposed to tell them that they're wrong and that's the way you talk to them.

So anyway we patched that up and didn't think anymore about it, so when Harry Burns had booked us, two of the dates were in Lake Charles, Louisiana, playing a dance, it was one of these little holes in the wall but it was a pretty nice little dance. So I went into the theme and I went to talking, saying good night and so on and so forth and so when

I got to the good night, a guy walks in front of the bandstand and said, what are you talking about? I said the dance is closed. You're not going to stop this dance, nigger. I said it's already stopped. I took the band off, and he pulled out a pearl handle forty five and he said you better go and play. I said you're not going to stop me because I just came in here (inaudible) and of course people came around and grabbed him. Somebody signalled to the man at the door and he came on down and grabbed the man and said, hey wait a minute, you're wrong, if you don't think you got your money's worth, I'll give you your money back, but the time is over for the band.
So he just shook his head and went on and mumbled and went off.
So Rene then said to me, I guess you see what I'm talking about.
want to come south with you.
